September 11 changed our city, our country, and countless lives forever.

Today, I remember every family who lost someone they loved, every survivor who carries the memories of that day, and every first responder who ran toward danger to save others.

We will never forget. https://t.co/PUWhF0lxzP

My heart is with the Kingsbridge residents impacted by today's four-alarm fire. I'm grateful to the firefighters who worked through difficult conditions to contain the blaze and helped ensure that there were no serious injuries. 

My office is following the situation closely. Residents who need assistance can reach out to us or contact the Red Cross at 1-800-RED-CROSS.

For the first time in more than 100 years, a North American river otter has been spotted in the Bronx River!

This remarkable moment is a testament to decades of work by Bronx environmental activists and community leaders who fought to restore our river. We thank them for their dedication and celebrate this incredible milestone for the Bronx.
https://t.co/A8KEhiLwe1

A third person held at Delaney Hall, Jose Chajon-Raxon, has now died after ICE released him to a hospital.

ICE says it has no responsibility because he was no longer in custody.

That’s exactly the loophole our bill, the Families Deserve to Know Act, closes. ICE should not be able to release someone and then evade responsibility for what happens to them shortly after.

https://t.co/3JfcNWVdnl
posts.summary: Criticizes ICE liability loophole, backs legislation to hold agency accountable
